To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) Fes is localized in both the cytoplasm and the nucleus of HL60 and K562 cells and only in the periphery of the nucleus of COS1 cells; (b) the treatment with differentiation inducers is followed by an increased amount of oligomeric form in the nucleus of myeloid cells; (c) oligomerization seems necessary for translocation, since Fes coiled-coil mutants are unable to form oligomers in the nucleus. (d)
the coiled-coils domains of the nonreceptor tyro-sine kinase p92c-FES are essential for nuclear localization of the protein upon induction of differentiation in myeloid leukemia cells.
the nuclear translocation of Fes requires its oligomerization through its coiled-coil domain, which is induced by the differentiation of myeloid cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the coiled coil domains in the nuclear translocation of Fes.
the study of the role of Fes in myeloid differentiation, focusing on its subcellular localization.
the study of Fes localization in myeloblasts and its regulation upon differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fes is localized in the nucleus upon differentiation of myeloid cells and that this translocation is oligomerization-dependent.
Fes localization in myelocytic cells is regulated by the coiled-coiled domain, whereas in COS cells, it is regulated by other domains.
the coiled-coils domains of Fes are necessary and sufficient to localize in the nuclei of myeloid cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fes localization in myelocytic cells is cell context dependent, and that nuclear localization is required for differentiation.
the oligomerization of Fes is a necessary step for nuclear translocation, but it is not sufficient, since the oligomers of Fes mutants lacking the coiled-coils do not localize in the nucleus.
Fes nuclear localization is induced by differentiation and that the coiled-coils domains are required for oligomerization and translocation to occur.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Fes localization is regulated by its oligomerization and that oligomerization is necessary to allow translocation of the protein to the nucleus.
Fes nuclear localization is cell type specific and that the coiled-coils are required for Fes oligomerization and translocation to the nucleus.
the nuclear translocation of p92cFes is a cell type-dependent event that is regulated by the coiled-coiled domains of the protein.
